summary: This sermon on Revelation 4-5 presents these chapters as the interpretive center of Revelation, revealing that Jesus the Lamb already sits enthroned through his sacrificial death and resurrection. The crisis facing the church is not whether Jesus might lose the throne, but whether believers will remember who sits on it and follow his way of conquering through faithful witness and sacrificial love rather than the empire's methods of power and violence.
key_points: The throne is occupied—God reigns now, not someday
John hears 'lion' but sees a 'slain lamb'—victory through sacrificial love
Worship participates in the heavenly reality where Christ's reign is already recognized
The church conquers by following the Lamb's pattern of faithful witness, even unto suffering
Communion is a pledge of allegiance to Christ above all earthly powers
big_idea: Jesus the Lamb already reigns on the throne through his sacrificial death and resurrection, and the church must pledge allegiance to him and conquer through faithful witness and sacrificial love rather than through the empire's methods of power and violence.
title: REVELATION: Pledge Allegiance to the Lamb
